root_cause.text: In `drivers/iommu/generic_pt` `DOMAIN_NS(unmap_pages)`, the IOTLB gather range was based on the requested unmap length `len` instead of the actual unmapped size `unmap.unmapped`, so when unmapping crossed into a large/contiguous IOPTE and removed more than requested, the invalidation range was too short.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that unmap "can unmap more than requested if the ending point lands within the middle of a large or contiguous IOPTE" and that "The gather was only flushing the range requested to be unmapped, not extending to the extra range"; the patch fixes this by changing `gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, len, ...)` to use `unmap.unmapped` instead of `len`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the actual unmapped length when gathering pages so cleanup and invalidation only apply to successfully unmapped mappings.
intent_record.what: The call to gather_range_pages() was changed so its fourth argument uses unmap.unmapped instead of len, while the function still returns unmap.unmapped.
intent_record.how: At runtime, page gathering for IOTLB invalidation/freeing now covers only the amount actually unmapped rather than the full requested length, preventing processing of pages outside the successfully unmapped range when fewer bytes/pages were removed than requested.

grouping_result.intent: Use the actual unmapped length when gathering pages so cleanup and invalidation only apply to successfully unmapped mappings.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it switches page gathering/invalidation from the requested unmap length to the actual unmapped size, ensuring IOTLB cleanup covers the full range actually unmapped.

candidates.rationale: This uses the requested unmap length `len` to gather the IOTLB invalidation range, instead of the actual unmapped size `unmap.unmapped`. If the unmap operation removes more than requested due to a larger contiguous mapping, the invalidation range becomes too short.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement gathers the IOTLB invalidation range using the requested unmap length `len` rather than the actual unmapped size. When the unmap operation removes a larger contiguous mapping and `unmap.unmapped` exceeds `len`, the gathered invalidation range is too short, leaving stale translations.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function body is sufficient because it shows both how the actual unmapped size is computed and how the IOTLB gather range is formed. The root cause says the bug occurs when the gather range uses the requested length instead of the actual unmapped size. In this code, `__unmap_range()` explicitly tracks the real amount removed in `unmap->unmapped`, including cases where a larger entry is removed than requested: the comment states `the entire entry is unmapped and the length returned will be larger than requested`, and the function accumulates this via `unmap->unmapped += log2_mul(num_oas, pt_table_item_lg2sz(&pts));`. However, `DOMAIN_NS(unmap_pages)` calls `gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, len, &unmap.free_list);` using `len = pgsize * pgcount`, i.e. the requested unmap length, not `unmap.unmapped`. Therefore, when unmapping removes more than requested due to a large/contiguous IOPTE, the invalidation range is too short. That is exactly the vulnerable construct. The fix would require using the actual unmapped size (`unmap.unmapped`) for the gather/invalidation range, but that is not present here.
